highlights.title: Show projected COB decay on Home chart
changes: The COB pane now displays a dashed orange curve and light area showing projected carb absorption into the future.
The projection extends from the latest determination and is bridged to recent data so the dashed curve connects to the歷.
The COB projection is refreshed whenever determinations update so it stays current.
The projected curve is adjusted to track the COB readout and avoid drifting above the displayed remaining carbs.
The COB projection is display-only and does not affect dosing or serialized determination output.

highlights.title: Clarify CGM smoothing description
changes: The CGM smoothing help text now says it requires 4 readings in a row, each arriving within 12 minutes of the prior one.
The text makes clear that only CGM readings are smoothed and manual entries are not changed.
Localized versions of the updated text were refreshed to match the clarification.

includedPullRequests.title: Plot Projected COB Decay in Home View Chart
includedPullRequests.body: ## Summary > [!IMPORTANT] > Depends on #1382 — this branch is based on it, so the diff shows its commits until it merges. Will be rebased onto dev afterwards; only the last commit is new here. Twin of #1382's IOB projection, for carbs: the COB pane now shows a dashed orange decay curve of forecasted carb absorption from "now" into the future. ### Decay Calculation The series is derived inside forecastCOB from the exact carb-impact terms that already makes up the COB-specific forecast. The linearly decaying observed carb impact plus the remaining-carbs triangle, divided by CSF, gives grams absorbed per 5-minute step, 48 values make up a 4 hours forecast. Subtracting from mealCOB (floored at 0) yields remaining COB per step. TODO: In a follow-up PR, refactor this to core data so per-cycle outputs become replayable. ### Additional Notes This is oref's own (crude) absorption model (linear carb impact decay and “triangle”-like instant decay, with a 30 g/hr cap), recomputed each cycle from observed deviations. The curve subsequently reshapes between algorithm runs. It shows what the algorithm currently “believes", not necessarily physiological prediction.
